title: Units, Measurement & Estimation
summary: Physics rests on SI units, dimensional consistency, significant figures, and order-of-magnitude estimates. Every equation must balance units, and unit conversions use ratios that cancel to leave the target unit.

SI units.plain: The standard metric base units of physics.
SI units.in_class: meter (m), kilogram (kg), second (s), and derived units like N, J, W.

dimension.plain: The physical type of a quantity (length, time, mass).
dimension.in_class: Both sides of a valid equation share the same dimensions.

dimensional analysis.plain: Checking or deriving relations by their units.
dimensional analysis.in_class: If units don't match, the equation is wrong.

significant figures.plain: The meaningful digits in a measurement.
significant figures.in_class: The answer's precision can't exceed the least-precise input.

unit conversion.plain: Rewriting a quantity in different units.
unit conversion.in_class: Multiply by ratios equal to 1 so unwanted units cancel.

order of magnitude.plain: The nearest power of ten of a quantity.
order of magnitude.in_class: For quick estimates and sanity checks.

scientific notation.in_class: Keeps track of very large or small values.

concept_sections.heading: SI base units
concept_sections.explanation: All mechanical quantities build from meter, kilogram, and second. Derived units combine them: velocity is m/s, force is $\mathrm{kg\cdot m/s}^2=\text{N}$, energy is $\mathrm{N\cdot m}=\text{J}$.
math_steps: Name the derived unit (N, J, W…).

concept_sections.heading: Dimensional analysis
concept_sections.explanation: Every term in an equation must have the same dimensions. Checking units catches errors and can even reveal the form of a relation up to a constant.

concept_sections.heading: Unit conversion
concept_sections.explanation: Multiply by conversion ratios (each equal to 1) arranged so the unwanted units cancel and the desired unit remains.
math_steps: Multiply by ratios that cancel unwanted units.

concept_sections.heading: Significant figures
concept_sections.explanation: Report only as many digits as your least-precise measurement justifies. Multiplication/division keeps the fewest sig figs; addition keeps the fewest decimal places.
math_steps: Count sig figs in each input.
For ×/÷ keep the fewest sig figs.

concept_sections.heading: Estimation
concept_sections.explanation: An order-of-magnitude estimate rounds each quantity to the nearest power of ten and combines them — a fast reality check on any calculation.
math_steps: Round inputs to powers of ten.
